Service: Infliximab infusion  
Date of Service: September 13, 2026, September 27, 2026, October 11, 2026  

Dear Appeals Coordinator,

I am writing to formally request an internal appeal of the denial for claim number 2026-PA-118734, dated October 26, 2026, which stated: "This claim has been denied because prior authorization was not obtained before the services were provided, as required for specialty infusion medications."

Under Section 5.2 Prior Authorization of the Cascade Community Health Plan policy, retrospective authorization will be granted when the service would have been approved had prior authorization been requested and the provider submits documentation within 90 days of the date of service. The Infusion Center Note dated September 8, 2026 confirms that a prior authorization request was faxed to Cascade on September 8, 2026 (confirmation #F-882173), five days before the September 13, 2026 infusion. To address concerns regarding completeness and receipt, we enclose: (1) the fax transmission report showing successful delivery to Cascade’s receiving fax number ([[FAX NUMBER]]) with timestamp and page count; and (2) the complete prior-authorization request packet, including the cover sheet, clinical notes documenting ileocolonic Crohn's disease, treatment plan specifying infliximab 5 mg/kg every 8 weeks, and laboratory results supporting ongoing therapy assessment.

Regarding the discretionary language in Section 5.2 ("may review"), we demonstrate that the service would have been approved had prior authorization been timely processed by mapping each Section 6.1 Crohn's Disease Biologic Therapy criterion to the submitted records: (a) infliximab is requested for moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease, supported by the September 6, 2026 gastroenterology note confirming ileocolonic involvement and clinical severity consistent with moderate-to-severe disease; (b) the patient had an inadequate response to, or intolerance of, at least one conventional therapy, specifically azathioprine from 2020 to 2022 discontinued due to hepatotoxicity, as documented in the same note; and (c) the patient has sustained remission on infliximab 5 mg/kg every 8 weeks since 2023 under Evergreen Health, establishing medical necessity and expected therapeutic benefit.

Furthermore, Section 5.3 Continuity of Care provides that members receiving an ongoing course of treatment under a previous health plan at the time of enrollment may continue that treatment for up to 90 days while prior authorization is obtained. The Gastroenterology Note from Dr. Helen Park dated September 6, 2026 confirms ongoing infliximab therapy since 2023 under Evergreen Health, with Cascade Community Health Plan effective August 13, 2026. All three infusions in question—September 13, September 27, and October 11, 2026—fall within the 90-day continuity-of-care window ending November 10, 2026, qualifying for continued coverage during the authorization process.

Given the patient’s stable three-year history on infliximab and the high risk of flare and antibody formation associated with interruption—as explicitly noted in the September 6, 2026 gastroenterology record—I request an expedited appeal under Section 10.1 Appeals, which allows for a decision within 72 hours when the standard timeframe could seriously jeopardize the member's health.

I respectfully request that Cascade Community Health Plan overturn the denial, authorize and pay for the infliximab infusions administered on September 13, 2026, September 27, 2026, and October 11, 2026, and provide a peer-to-peer review upon request. Please also provide a full copy of the claim file and the clinical criteria used in the original denial determination.

Enclosures:  
1. Fax transmission report confirming delivery of the prior authorization request to Cascade on September 8, 2026 (receiving fax number: [[FAX NUMBER]], timestamp, page count)  
2. Complete prior-authorization request packet faxed September 8, 2026 (cover sheet, clinical notes, lab results, treatment plan)  
3. Medical records showing continuous infliximab use since 2023 and failure of azathioprine due to hepatotoxicity
